title: Navigation API: An event for when entries disappear for reasons other than forward-pruning

body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#72 — filed by @domenic (2021-03). 12 comments.

---

`dispose` fires when entries are dropped due to forward-pruning. But entries can disappear for several other reasons, and apps currently get no notification:

- **The user clears their history**, removing entries from the joint session history.
- **The browser's entry limit is hit** (Chrome's is 50), so entries drop off the back.
- **The list gets "cut in half"**, e.g.:
  - history is `/1`, `/2`, `/3`, all in bfcache
  - user goes back to `/2`
  - the page does `location.replace("https://other.example.com/")`
  - traversing back to `/1` now sees **1** entry instead of the 3 it saw before, because only one same-origin contiguous run remains

The last case is the interesting one: an app that cached `key` values or reasoned about `entries()` length can silently be wrong, with no event to react to. Since a stated goal of the navigation API is that state is never unexpectedly lost, this is arguably a correctness gap rather than a nice-to-have.

Related: WICG/navigation-api#205 (a general `entrieschange` event) was proposed partly as a cleaner way to cover these cases.

cc @domenic
